## PyFFmpegCore {{ tag }}: verifiable managed FFmpeg workflows

PyFFmpegCore remains a local-first beta. FFmpeg and FFprobe stay explicit
system dependencies. This release strengthens the inspect → execute → verify
flow without claiming that metadata probing is a full decode or a sandbox.

### What changed

- Managed jobs verify that declared outputs exist, are non-empty, and are
  readable by FFprobe when available. Missing or invalid outputs fail
  validation; unavailable FFprobe is reported as unverified.
- Built-in profiles check their promised codecs, stream types, pixel format,
  and selected subtitle language against output probe facts.
- `convert --preserve-all-streams` compares input and output stream types,
  codecs, and languages; receipts retain the comparison evidence.
- Plans warn when default stream selection omits additional tracks. Human probe
  output lists every stream and labels differing frame rates as a VFR clue.
- Accessibility subtitle language is supported in the profile and versioned
  batch manifest schema 1.1; schema 1.0 remains supported.
- Subprocess text uses explicit UTF-8 decoding with replacement across the
  runner and release helpers.

### Verification

- Exact release wheel build and six OS/Python artifact checks: [release workflow]({{ release_run_url }})
- [Compatibility policy](https://othmaneblial.github.io/pyffmpegcore/COMPATIBILITY/)
- Historical synthetic recipe evidence from public `0.2.2`: [measurements and receipts](https://othmaneblial.github.io/pyffmpegcore/evidence/)
- [Full changelog](https://github.com/OthmaneBlial/pyffmpegcore/compare/v0.2.2...v0.3.0)

The FFprobe checks cover readable container metadata and documented profile
contracts. They do not decode every packet or frame, and remote or unprobeable
inputs can remain unverified. No hostile-media sandbox is claimed.
